page.layout: One block of running text in a single column, with a large woodcut initial A at the upper left; page number centred at the head. No margin notes, no running head, no catchword.

main_text.l: A Thenis, celeberrimæ cui civitati
ac Reipublicæ omnium artium
ac disciplinarum, natales & incu-
nabula debentur, moris fuisse ex
antiquitate constat, ut, qui ma-
gnis vellet imbui mysteriis, quod aliquandiu ne-
mini licebat, parvis ante imbueretur. Cujus qui-
dem instituti, nisi hallucinor, hæc est ratio, quod
paulatim ad majora veniendum judicarent,
&, in sacris quoque divinisque rebus, ordinem na-
turæ comprobarent: sive quòd indignum ali-
quem putarent, qui ad absoluta aut majora grad-
uaretur sacra, nisi in minori præparatum rectè
prius animum haberet. Utrisq; vero initiatum
rebus omnibus florentem ac ornatum, ad extre-
mam usq; senectutem, ac post hanc vitam, con-
sortio Deorum, piarumque animarum insitum
fore autumabant. Quod in sacris Athenienses
faciendum judicabant, id in artibus & discipli-
nis, quibus omnis nostra vita constat, omnis
nostræ ratio felicitatis continetur, quas myste-
ria

page.notes: The woodcut initial "A" is decorative and joined to "Thenis". Line "graf-saretur" reads as printed "graf- saretur" (likely graduaretur/ graffaretur); the word at the line end "graf-" with following "saretur" is transcribed as printed in the scan and may be misread: "graf[?]". Text continues on the next page ("ria" at the bottom right is the catchword-like fragment of the word "mysteria" split across pages; it is printed as a line-end word).
